name: Otaru Aquarium
closed: Seasonal closures between winter and spring seasons
access: Bus from JR Otaru Station (Otaru-ekimae terminal, stand 3)
highlight: Sea-facing outdoor pools with seals and sea lions right on the coast

name: Shin-Sapporo Sunpiazza Aquarium
ja: 新さっぽろサンピアザ水族館
access: 3 min walk from JR Shin-Sapporo / 5 min from subway Shin-Sapporo
highlight: Small city aquarium inside a shopping complex; easy add-on in Sapporo

name: AOAO SAPPORO
access: 3 min walk from Odori Station (all three subway lines)
highlight: Urban night-time aquarium in the Moyuk Sapporo tower; penguins on an upper floor

name: Noboribetsu Marine Park Nixe
ja: 登別マリンパークニクス
access: 5 min walk from JR Noboribetsu Station
highlight: Danish-castle-style building; daily penguin parade

name: Chitose Aquarium (Salmon Hometown)
ja: サケのふるさと 千歳水族館
access: 15 min walk from JR Chitose Station; 15 min by car from New Chitose Airport
highlight: Underwater windows into the actual Chitose River — wild salmon run in autumn

name: Oga Aquarium GAO
access: Bus from JR Oga Station
highlight: Polar bears and the Sea of Japan coast; hata-hata (sailfin sandfish) local exhibit

name: Kamo Aquarium (Tsuruoka)
access: Bus from JR Tsuruoka Station (about 40 min) to Kamo Suizokukan
highlight: The jellyfish aquarium — dozens of species and a 5 m jellyfish tank

name: Aquamarine Fukushima
ja: アクアマリンふくしま
access: Bus from JR Izumi Station to Aeon Mall Iwaki Onahama, then 5 min walk
highlight: Triangular tunnel tank where the Kuroshio and Oyashio currents meet; sanma (saury) breeding

name: Inawashiro Kawasemi Aquarium
ja: アクアマリンいなわしろカワセミ水族館
access: About 10 min by taxi from JR Inawashiro Station
highlight: Freshwater life of Lake Inawashiro and its rivers; kingfishers

name: Kamogawa Sea World
closed: Some weekdays in low season (see calendar)
access: Free shuttle bus about 10 min from JR Awa-Kamogawa Station
highlight: Orca performances — one of only three places in Japan with orcas (with Nagoya and Kobe Suma)

name: Saitama Aquarium
closed: About one Monday a month; none in August
access: About 15 min by taxi from Tobu Hanyu or Kazo Station
highlight: Freshwater only — the fish of Saitama's rivers, in a park with lotus ponds

name: Sunshine Aquarium
hours: Varies by day (see calendar); last entry 30 min before closing
closed: A few maintenance days a year (e.g. 12 Nov 2026)
access: Sunshine City, Ikebukuro
highlight: Rooftop 'Sunshine Aqua Ring' where sea lions swim overhead

name: Tokyo Sea Life Park (Kasai)
access: 5 min walk from JR Kasai-Rinkai-Koen Station (Keiyo Line)
highlight: Doughnut tank of schooling bluefin tuna; run by the Tokyo Zoological Park Society

name: Shinagawa Aquarium
access: 8 min walk from Keikyu Omori-Kaigan Station
highlight: Ward-run aquarium with a tunnel tank and dolphin pool; good value in Tokyo

name: Maxell Aqua Park Shinagawa
ja: マクセル アクアパーク品川
access: Inside Shinagawa Prince Hotel, 2 min walk from JR Shinagawa Station
highlight: Sound-and-light dolphin show; date-night aquarium next to Shinagawa Station

name: HANA-BIYORI (Yomiuriland)
adult_note: HANA-BIYORI garden entry; ¥2,300 with the hot-spring set
access: Free shuttle from Odakyu Shin-Yurigaoka Station
highlight: Aquarium tanks inside a flower greenhouse — the JAZA member is Yomiuriland

name: Sumida Aquarium
access: Direct from Oshiage (Skytree-mae) Station, 5 min
highlight: Open-air Magellanic penguin pool indoors; Ogasawara-themed tank; jellyfish lab

name: Kawasaki Aquarium (Kawasui)
ja: カワスイ 川崎水族館
access: Right outside JR Kawasaki Station east exit
highlight: River-themed — Tama River to the Amazon; capybaras and a rainforest zone

name: Yokohama Hakkeijima Sea Paradise
ja: 横浜・八景島シーパラダイス
adult_note: Aqua Resorts Pass (four aquarium facilities); rides extra
access: Seaside Line Hakkeijima Station
highlight: Four aquarium buildings on one island, plus rides — a full-day resort

name: Tochigi Nakagawa Aquarium
ja: 栃木県なかがわ水遊園
closed: Mondays (open daily in Golden Week and mid-Jul–Aug)
access: About 40 min by bus from JR Nishi-Nasuno Station
highlight: Freshwater aquarium built around the Naka River; big Amazon tunnel tank

name: Mori no Naka no Suizokukan (Yamanashi Fuji Aquarium)
ja: 森の中の水族館。山梨県立富士湧水の里水族館
access: 3 min walk from Sakana-Koen bus stop (Fujikyu bus)
highlight: Freshwater aquarium fed by Fuji spring water — a two-layer 'double doughnut' tank

name: Niigata City Aquarium Marinepia Nihonkai
ja: 新潟市水族館 マリンピア日本海
closed: 29 Dec–1 Jan; first Thu of March and the next day
access: Bus from Niigata Station to Suizokukan-mae
highlight: Sea of Japan marine life; dolphin shows on the coast

name: Joetsu Aquarium Umigatari
ja: 上越市立水族博物館 うみがたり
access: Joetsu city (Naoetsu area)
highlight: One of Japan's largest Magellanic penguin colonies; infinity-edge tank facing the Sea of Japan

name: Teradomari Aquarium
closed: About one day a month plus 31 Dec–2 Jan
access: Teradomari fishing-port area, Nagaoka
highlight: Small octagonal aquarium on the water beside the Teradomari fish market

name: Notojima Aquarium
access: Bus from JR Wakura-Onsen Station
highlight: Whale shark tank on Noto Island; reopened after the 2024 earthquake

name: Tokai University Marine Science Museum
ja: 東海大学海洋科学博物館
access: Miho, Shizuoka
highlight: Still a JAZA member but no longer open to walk-in visitors — do not plan a trip around it

name: Hekinan Seaside Aquarium
access: About 15 min walk from Hekinan Station (Meitetsu)
highlight: City aquarium of about 300 species from Japan's coasts; conservation of endangered freshwater fish

name: Port of Nagoya Public Aquarium
access: 5 min walk from Nagoyako Station (subway Meiko Line), exit 3
highlight: Japan's largest pool for dolphin performances; orcas and belugas; penguins of Antarctica

name: SEA LIFE Nagoya
access: 10 min walk from Kinjo-futo Station (Aonami Line)
highlight: Compact family aquarium next to LEGOLAND Japan

name: Lake Biwa Museum
ja: 滋賀県立琵琶湖博物館
access: Bus about 25 min from JR Kusatsu Station west exit
highlight: A museum whose aquarium wing shows the endemic fish of Lake Biwa — Japan's oldest lake

name: Kyoto Aquarium
access: 7 min walk from JR Umekoji-Kyotonishi; 15 min from Kyoto Station
highlight: Japanese giant salamanders in the 'River of Kyoto' zone; jellyfish and penguins

name: Toba Aquarium
access: About 10 min walk from JR/Kintetsu Toba Station
highlight: The only dugong on display in Japan; roughly 1,200 species, no fixed route

name: Ise Sea Paradise
closed: A few inspection days a year
access: Bus from Ise-shi Station to Meoto-Iwa Higashiguchi (about 46 min)
highlight: Hands-on with sea lions, walruses and otters, next to the Meoto Iwa 'wedded rocks'

name: Osaka Aquarium Kaiyukan
closed: A few days a year (see calendar)
access: 5 min walk from Osakako Station (Osaka Metro Chuo Line), exit 1
highlight: Whale sharks in the 9 m-deep Pacific Ocean tank; 'Ring of Fire' route around the Pacific

name: NIFREL
access: Osaka Monorail Bampaku-Kinen-Koen Station (Expocity)
highlight: Kaiyukan's 'living museum' — small tanks lit like art, plus a white tiger and free-roaming birds

name: Kobe Suma Sea World
ja: 神戸須磨シーワールド
access: Suma Kaihin Koen area, Kobe
highlight: Opened 2024 — orcas in western Japan; dolphin stadium on Suma beach

name: átoa (Aquarium × Art)
access: About 20 min walk from Sannomiya / Motomachi
highlight: Aquarium as art installation — spherical tank and projection rooms

name: Kinosaki Marine World
closed: A few days a year (see calendar)
access: About 10 min by bus from JR Kinosaki-Onsen Station
highlight: Sea-cliff aquarium near Kinosaki Onsen; catch-your-own aji fishing

name: Himeji City Aquarium
access: Tegarayama Central Park, Himeji
highlight: Local Harima-coast species and freshwater fish; a quiet, cheap add-on to Himeji Castle

name: Tamano Marine Museum (Shibukawa)
ja: 玉野海洋博物館（渋川マリン水族館）
closed: One weekday a week (none in summer)
access: Bus from JR Uno Station (about 30 min)
highlight: Small Seto Inland Sea aquarium on Shibukawa beach

name: Miyajima Public Aquarium
access: Walk from Miyajima ferry pier past Itsukushima Shrine
highlight: Finless porpoises of the Seto Inland Sea; oyster-farming exhibit

name: Shimane Aquarium AQUAS
ja: しまね海洋館アクアス
access: Bus from JR Hamada Station to Aquas-mae; or walk from JR Hashi Station
highlight: Beluga whales blowing bubble rings

name: Katsurahama Aquarium
access: Bus about 30 min from JR Kochi Station to Katsurahama
highlight: Beach-side aquarium famous online for its irreverent mascot; pets allowed

name: Osakana-kan (Morinokuni)
access: 3 min walk from JR Matsumaru Station (Yodo Line)
highlight: Freshwater fish of the Shimanto River basin, in a roadside station

name: Marine World Uminonakamichi
ja: マリンワールド海の中道
closed: Four days from the third Monday of January
access: JR Kashii Line to Uminonakamichi Station
highlight: Kyushu's seas — a huge sardine school tank and dolphin/sea-lion show over Hakata Bay

name: Oita Marine Palace Aquarium Umitamago
ja: 大分マリーンパレス水族館 うみたまご
access: Bus from JR Beppu or Oita Station (Takasakiyama-mae)
highlight: Touch pools and walrus/dolphin shows; next door to the Takasakiyama monkey park

name: Kagoshima City Aquarium (Io World)
ja: いおワールドかごしま水族館
closed: Four days from the first Monday of December
access: Streetcar to Suizokukan-guchi, then 8 min walk
highlight: Whale shark in the Kuroshio tank; sea life of the Nansei islands

name: Nagasaki Penguin Aquarium
access: Bus from Nagasaki Station toward Aba / Kasuga-shako-mae
highlight: Nine penguin species — one of the most in the world; penguins on a natural beach

name: Okinawa Churaumi Aquarium
access: Expressway bus from Naha (about 2 h) to Ocean Expo Park
highlight: Whale sharks and mantas in the Kuroshio Sea tank; the aquarium that tops every list
